id_and_class.theory_title: Broad’s Emergent Mind and Psychic/Psi Factors
id_and_class.summary: C. D. Broad argued that phenomenal qualities are real and cannot be deduced from even complete physical knowledge of the brain, so consciousness is a strongly emergent property of organized matter linked to it by irreducible ‘trans-ordinal’ laws. On ordinary evidence he favored this Emergent Materialism, but he held that well-established psychical phenomena would support a Compound Theory, in which mind emerges from a brain combined with a further ‘psychic factor’ that might outlast the body.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as Strongly Emergent, Perhaps With a Psychic Factor

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is a genuinely novel characteristic that emerges, by lawful but non-deducible trans-ordinal laws, from suitably organized material systems, possibly in compound with a non-observable psychic factor.
conceptual_ground.ontological_status: Emergent materialism (strong), open to a psychic factor
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Mental properties depend lawfully on brain organization yet cannot be reduced to or predicted from physical properties. In the Compound Theory, the conscious mind belongs to the organized combination of brain and psychic factor, not to either one alone.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Strong emergence (connected to its physical base by trans-ordinal laws that are discovered empirically and cannot be deduced from below)
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Perception has an immediately presented sensory content (a sensum) and an ‘external reference’ to a world beyond it, as when a tilted circular coin presents an elliptical sensum yet is seen as round. Broad later called the basic relation of sensory presentation ‘prehension’.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Qualia are real and irreducible. Broad’s ‘mathematical archangel’, with complete knowledge of ammonia molecules, receptors, and brain, could deduce ammonia’s microstructure but not its smell, which is known only by experiencing it.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Material systems at many levels of organization; emergent mental characteristics; trans-ordinal psychophysical laws; possibly a psychic factor (later called the Ψ-component) carrying part of a person’s dispositional basis.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: First-person acquaintance with one’s own experiences, which Broad treated as data any metaphysics must preserve, combined with science and, conditionally, psychical research.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Experience includes qualitative sensory content, external reference, and temporal organization such as the specious present. Personality consists largely of dispositions (memories, traits, skills) grounded in some persisting structure.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal, Perception, Temporal experience, Personality and memory, Psi and survival
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Trans-ordinal laws: the link between a level of organization and the properties that emerge at it is a basic law of nature, found only by observing the emergent property after it appears.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: Consciousness appears when material constituents reach a sufficient level of organization, and its qualitative character follows lawfully from that configuration.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: In living brains and nervous systems; on the Compound Theory, partly in a psychic factor not open to ordinary observation.
core_claims_and_evidence: Broad mapped exactly seventeen possible mind-matter theories by asking whether mentality and materiality are each fundamental, emergent, reducible, or delusive, then eliminated them by argument.
Any theory that calls mentality an illusion refutes itself, since an illusion is already a mental seeming.

Psychical phenomena such as telepathy and precognition would violate ‘basic limiting principles’, including the privacy of minds and their dependence on living brains, so psi is the main empirical test of those assumptions.
A Ψ-component might carry part of a person’s dispositional structure after death without itself being a person or having experiences, which may still require a living organism.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Philosophical (conceptual analysis and systematic taxonomy), phenomenological, and conditionally empirical (psychical research)

empirics_and_critiques.known_empirical_interventions_or_tests: ESP card-guessing experiments, notably S. G. Soal’s, and studies of mediumship, telepathy, clairvoyance, precognition, and apparitions. Broad set a procedure of first excluding fraud, error, coincidence, sensory leakage, and known causes.
empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Broad leaned heavily on Soal’s experiments, which Betty Markwick later showed involved data manipulation. He dismissed psychokinesis and physical mediumship on thin grounds, and Chalmers notes that the archangel argument ignores the option of an epistemic gap without an ontological one.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: The nature of the psychic factor is left open, and Broad stresses that its persistence after death would not amount to survival of the person, which would need continuity of memory, character, and cognitive organization.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Broad regarded the Compound Theory as possibly compatible with Emergent Materialism, depending on what the psychic factor turns out to be. McLaughlin treats him as the culmination of British emergentism.

AI_consciousness.rationale: Since mentality emerges by trans-ordinal laws that can only be found by observation, whether an artificial organization would produce experience cannot be deduced in advance.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: Broad held that a psychic factor carrying some dispositions might persist after death if psychical evidence is genuine, but he did not claim this established, and such persistence would fall short of personal survival.
